Tg: Glass transition temperature of the electrolyte (polymer plus dissolved salt) — the temperature below which it stiffens from a rubbery to a glassy state.
Li:functional group: Molar ratio of lithium ions to the polymer's coordinating functional groups — how concentrated the dissolved salt is.
Conductivity at 30C: Ionic conductivity of the electrolyte measured at 30°C.
Conductivity at 60C: Ionic conductivity of the electrolyte measured at 60°C.
Conductivity at 90C: Ionic conductivity of the electrolyte measured at 90°C.
Comonomer1 apol: Atomic polarizability of comonomer 1 — how easily its electron cloud distorts in an electric field.
Comonomer1 Vabc: Van der Waals volume of comonomer 1 — an estimate of the molecule's physical size.
Comonomer2 apol: Atomic polarizability of comonomer 2 — how easily its electron cloud distorts in an electric field.
Comonomer2 Vabc: Van der Waals volume of comonomer 2 — an estimate of the molecule's physical size.
anion apol: Atomic polarizability of the anion — how easily its electron cloud distorts in an electric field.
anion Vabc: Van der Waals volume of the anion — an estimate of the ion's physical size.
Arrhenius Ea (eV): Activation energy for ion transport from a simple Arrhenius fit, in electron-volts — how much energy ions need to start moving through the polymer.
VFT activation energy (K): Activation-energy-like term from a Vogel-Fulcher-Tammann (VFT) fit, in Kelvin. VFT is used instead of a simple Arrhenius law because conductivity rises faster than Arrhenius predicts as a polymer approaches its glass transition.
VFT activation energy with fixed T0 (K): Same VFT activation-energy term, but from a fit where the reference temperature T0 was held fixed rather than allowed to vary freely.
Arrhenius prefactor (S/cm): Pre-exponential term from the Arrhenius fit — the conductivity the fit extrapolates to at infinitely high temperature.
VFT prefactor (S/cm*T^(1/2)): Pre-exponential term from the VFT fit, scaled by the square root of temperature.
VFT prefactor with set T0: VFT pre-exponential term from the fit where T0 was held fixed.
Transference number: Fraction of the total ionic current carried by the lithium ion rather than its counter-ion — higher generally means better battery performance.
drying temp: Temperature the sample was dried at during preparation, to drive off residual casting solvent.
Polymer family: Chemical family of the polymer's backbone (e.g. ether, ester, carbonate).
Polymer: Name of the specific polymer used as the electrolyte host.
Anion: The lithium salt's counter-ion (e.g. TFSI, ClO4), paired with the Li+ cation that actually carries charge.
Solvent used: Solvent the polymer was dissolved/cast in during sample preparation.
Conductivity at 0C: Ionic conductivity of the electrolyte measured at 0°C.
Conductivity at 15C: Ionic conductivity of the electrolyte measured at 15°C.
Conductivity at 20C: Ionic conductivity of the electrolyte measured at 20°C.
Conductivity at 21C: Ionic conductivity of the electrolyte measured at 21°C.
Conductivity at 25C: Ionic conductivity of the electrolyte measured at 25°C (approximately room temperature).
Conductivity at 27C: Ionic conductivity of the electrolyte measured at 27°C.
Conductivity at 35C: Ionic conductivity of the electrolyte measured at 35°C.
Conductivity at 40C: Ionic conductivity of the electrolyte measured at 40°C.
Conductivity at 45C: Ionic conductivity of the electrolyte measured at 45°C.
Conductivity at 50C: Ionic conductivity of the electrolyte measured at 50°C.
Conductivity at 55C: Ionic conductivity of the electrolyte measured at 55°C.
Conductivity at 65C: Ionic conductivity of the electrolyte measured at 65°C.
Conductivity at 70C: Ionic conductivity of the electrolyte measured at 70°C.
Conductivity at 75C: Ionic conductivity of the electrolyte measured at 75°C.
Conductivity at 80C: Ionic conductivity of the electrolyte measured at 80°C.
Conductivity at 85C: Ionic conductivity of the electrolyte measured at 85°C.
Conductivity at 100C: Ionic conductivity of the electrolyte measured at 100°C.
Conductivity at 110C: Ionic conductivity of the electrolyte measured at 110°C.
Conductivity at 125C: Ionic conductivity of the electrolyte measured at 125°C.
Tg polymer without salt: Glass transition temperature of the bare polymer, measured before any lithium salt is added.
Polymer Mn (kDa): Number-average molecular weight of the polymer (kDa) — reflects the typical chain length.
Polymer Mw (kDa): Weight-average molecular weight of the polymer (kDa) — weighted toward longer chains than Mn, so it's more sensitive to a few very long chains.
Comonomer percentage: Percentage of the minority comonomer making up the copolymer.
DOI: Digital Object Identifier — a permanent link to the published paper this sample's data came from.
Reference: Full citation for the paper this sample was reported in.
Notes: Free-text notes recorded by the original curators about this sample.
SMILES descriptor 1: SMILES string — a compact text notation encoding comonomer 1's molecular structure.
SMILES descriptor 2: SMILES string — a compact text notation encoding comonomer 2's molecular structure.
